ScenarioThe blood uses a bicarbonate buffer system. CO2 is released by respiration in your tissues and is dissolved in your blood stream. The enzyme in your blood, carbonic anhydrase, converts water and carbon dioxide into carbonic acid, which then readily dissociates into hydrogen ions and bicarbonate. This decrease in pH is what helps hemoglobin release oxygen in your tissues.
Write the equation that describes the equilibrium constant (Keq) for the chemical reaction catalyzed by carbonic anhydrase: CO2 + H2O ⇌ H2CO3.
Keq = [H2CO3] / [CO2][H2O] = [products]/[reactants]
*Note: These are the concentrations of products and reactants AT EQUILIBRIUM!
Her extra reasoning (slide notes)
To find the equilibrium constant of any reaction, it will be the products over the reactants. The gases are included for reactions that take place in organisms since they’re dissolved in the solution and do not immediately evaporate from the system. Note that T and R will always be the same when calculating Keq R because R is always the gas constant. T because Keq implies standard state conditions, which locks the temp @25C Temp can change when calculating ΔG, but for ΔG°’ it will always be the same due to the definition of standard state. If you struggle to determine the effect of Keq on delta G, look at what happens when you plug generic numbers into full equation. Don’t get confused: Standard temperature and pressure (STP): 0°C, 1atm of pressure Used more in chemistry Standard State Conditions: 25°C, pH 7.0, all reactant/product concentrations start at 1M Used more in biochemistry/biology
